newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian riots spread despite state of emergency.
newsitem.headline: Albanian riots spread despite state of emergency.

text.p: Violent protests flared across Albania on Sunday as rioters vented their anger against President Sali Berisha's right-wing government and defied a national state of emergency.
In the main southern town of Gjirokaster, rioters sprayed a police station with bullets from Kalashnikov assault rifles and then set it ablaze, witnesses said.
Police fled as up to 30 masked raiders attacked the building. Flames rose up soon afterwards and the crackle of automatic gunfire mixed with the din of ambulance sirens.
"I can see flames and smoke rising from the police station," one witness said.

It was not clear if there were any casualties in the violence, which broke out after parliament voted to impose a state of emergency to try to end rioting unleashed by the failure in January of shady savings schemes.
Officials at the Greek consulate, the only foreign representation in Gjirokaster, said they had asked for police protection.

President Sali Berisha, reeling from a popular backlash against the dubious pyramid schemes, vowed to quash unrest But it showed no signs of ebbing despite the resignation on Saturday of right-wing Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi.

"Armed communist rebels helped and finance by foreign espionage services have started military actions to overthrow the government with force and establish their rule across the country," Berisha said in a televised address.
"They will very soon feel the iron hand and the full punishment of the laws," he declared.

Rioters have captured security forces' weapons in a series of raids on police and military installations. A police officer in Gjirokaster said he believed rebels there seized their guns from a police arms depot in the village of Pitsari, about 20 km (12 miles) to the north.

In northwest Albania, guards at Lezhe jail shot dead one prisoner and wounded three after the prisoners tried to use two hostage officials as human shields in a breakout attempt, the Justice Ministry said.
Earlier about 100 convicts succeeded in escaping from jail in the Adriatic town of Sarande, residents said.

Demonstrators cruised Sarande's streets in cars, shooting into the air with Kalashnikovs stolen from police headquarters. Youths could be seen breaking into banks and shops and six police vehicles burned in the main square.
"There are no injured because there were no clashes. The police have fled," an official at Sarande's hospital said.
The army barracks on the edge of the town, a sizeable minority of whose 20,000 residents are ethnic Greeks, was also deserted.

"Our commanding officers have fled. We don't know what to do. People stole about 400 Kalashnikovs from police headquarters. I'll try to make my way back to Tirana where my home is," said a lieutenant who gave his first name as Adrian.

Protest organisers in Vlore, scene of the worst bloodshed so far, demanded the dissolution of parliament and called on Berisha not to stand for re-election in a vote scheduled in the chamber on Monday.
Berisha's official villa in Vlore was among buildings pillaged by protesters. Witnesses said looters were carting off doors and windows and uprooting flowers from the garden.
